criteria.description: The server-rendered review dashboard presents every release pack in the requested timeline-and-cards layout.
verification: Start Release Manager and open the review interface in a browser.
Confirm every pack returned by the existing pack-list API appears once in the left timeline and once as a main-panel card, ordered newest first.
Confirm timeline dots are connected by a rail and the current pack, or newest pack when none is current, is visibly highlighted.
Confirm each card displays its version, status pill, and timestamped audit events.

criteria.description: A reviewer can open a pack and inspect all release content and supporting links.
verification: From the dashboard, open a pack's full review page.
Confirm the page shows version, changelog, release notes, announcement, and all supporting commit and pull-request links supplied by the API.
Activate one commit link and one pull-request link and confirm each resolves to its intended external URL.

criteria.description: Anyone with network access can approve a pending or in-progress pack with a reason, triggering publication.
verification: Without signing in, open a pending or in-progress pack and attempt approval with an empty or whitespace-only reason; confirm submission is blocked or rejected with a visible validation message.
Submit approval with a non-blank reason and confirm the publication workflow is triggered.

After publication completes, reload the page and query the same pack through the existing API; confirm its canonical status is published and its audit timeline contains the approval reason, publication outcome, and timestamps.
If publication fails, confirm a visible failure is shown and the pack is not falsely displayed as published.

criteria.description: Anyone with network access can reject a pending or in-progress pack with a reason.
verification: Without signing in, open a pending or in-progress pack and attempt rejection with an empty or whitespace-only reason; confirm submission is blocked or rejected with a visible validation message.
Submit rejection with a non-blank reason, reload the page, and confirm the pack is visibly rejected.
Query the same pack through the existing API and confirm its status is rejected and its audit timeline contains the rejection, reason, and timestamp.

criteria.description: Published packs show the requested release metrics while non-published packs do not present them as published results.
verification: View a published pack card and confirm it contains metric tiles for commit count, pull-request count, and changelog line count.
Confirm each tile uses a large bold numeric value with a smaller muted label.
Compare the displayed values with the pack data returned by the API.
View a non-published pack and confirm it does not display those metrics as published results.

criteria.description: The interface follows the specified minimalist, semantic-status visual design.
verification: Inspect the dashboard and full pack page at a desktop viewport.
Confirm a white background, sans-serif type, generous spacing, 1px card or section borders, and no card shadows.
Confirm pending or in-progress indicators are amber/orange, published or healthy indicators green, rejected or failed indicators red, and links blue.
Confirm decorative colors are not used for unrelated content.

criteria.description: The review flow remains usable as server-rendered FastAPI HTML and the product passes its required verification.
verification: Disable JavaScript in the browser, reload the review interface, and confirm packs can still be listed, opened, approved, and rejected through normal navigation and form submission.
Inspect browser network activity and confirm the initial review pages are HTML responses rather than a client-rendered SPA shell, with no frontend-framework runtime required.
Confirm operator documentation names GITHUB_TOKEN, GITHUB_OWNER, and GITHUB_REPO.
Run `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` from the repository root and confirm it exits successfully.

note: The definition of done. Later phases may ONLY flip `passes`. Editing or removing a criterion is a gate failure.
